{"id": "87d62482-f215-4f40-a14b-be2288165239", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "You have a lot of SSD headroom. At the current growth rate, you won't run out for decades.

The only ONTAP file system in this account (us-east-1) is `fsx-diag-ontap-maz2` (`fs-00000000000000001`). It's Multi-AZ, has 1,024 GiB of SSD provisioned, and is available.

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Usable SSD capacity | ~925 GB (~862 GiB) |
| SSD used (Nov 9) | ~2.39 GB (~0.26%) |
| SSD free | ~923 GB (~860 GiB) |
| Average growth, Nov 2 to Nov 9 | ~22 MB/day |
| Time to full at that rate | ~42,000 days (~115 years) |
| Time to 80% (the usual alert level) | ~34,000 days (~90+ years) |

- **Growth is slowing:** The daily increases were about 81, 25, 16, 12, 10, 5, and 3 MB. That looks like an initial data load tapering off, so the 22 MB/day average is probably an overestimate. Even the peak day (81 MB) would take about 31 years to fill the file system.
- **Short history:** CloudWatch only returned 8 days of SSD usage data (Nov 2 to Nov 9). Treat the projection as a rough estimate. A new workload, or a bulk data load, would change it.
- **Usable vs. provisioned:** The 925 GB figure is lower than the 1,024 GiB you provisioned because ONTAP reserves some of it.

To make this more useful, you could set a CloudWatch alarm on SSD utilization at about 80%. If you expect a large migration or a new workload, tell me the size and I'll re-run the projection with it included.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
